stem: What did the buffalo mean to the Plains peoples before the 1870s?

stimulus.source_note: Colonel Richard Dodge's 1871 description as quoted in HISTORY.com, "Why Is the Bison America's National Mammal?"; herd figures from the U.S. Geological Survey (about 20-30 million bison before the slaughter, barely more than 1,000 by 1889) and Hornaday's 1889 census count of 1,091.
stimulus.text:
"The whole country appeared one mass of buffalo," wrote Colonel Richard Dodge when he traveled the Santa Fe Trail in 1871.

(Background from the books: between 1871 and 1883, hide hunters working in teams killed millions of bison for their skins, and railroads carried the hides east. When the Smithsonian sent an expedition to Montana in 1886 to collect specimens from the vanishing herds, few remained; Hornaday's 1889 census counted only 1,091 bison left in all of North America.)

options.text: A sport animal hunted only for entertainment by tribal leaders
options.misconception: Background: the buffalo was the center of Plains life, not a sport animal; hunting it fed and clothed whole peoples.

options.text: The foundation of their way of life: food, shelter, tools, and spiritual meaning
A pest that destroyed their crops and had to be driven off
options.misconception: Background: Plains peoples were hunters, not settled crop farmers; the buffalo sustained them rather than threatening their fields.

options.text: A source of cash from selling hides to eastern factories
options.misconception: Background: the hide trade that destroyed the herds was run by white commercial hunters; Native peoples used the buffalo for their own needs, not for factory sales.

rationales.A: Background: the buffalo fed, clothed, and sheltered Plains peoples and stood at the center of their spiritual life. Sport hunting was the white hunters' business, not theirs.
rationales.B: Dodge's image says it: the whole country appeared one mass of buffalo. Background: the herds were the Plains peoples' food, shelter, tools, and ceremony in one animal.
rationales.C: Background: the Plains peoples lived by hunting the herds, not by farming fields the buffalo could ruin.
rationales.D: Background: the commercial hide trade belonged to white hunters working for eastern markets. Native peoples depended on the buffalo itself, not on selling it.
rationales.general:
One animal fed, clothed, housed, and taught a whole people.
1. Picture what Dodge saw: a country that appeared one mass of buffalo.
2. Ask what a people living among those herds got from them. Background: meat, hides, bones, and ceremony.
3. Name the role. The buffalo was not one resource among many; it was the foundation itself.
Remember: when one animal is food, house, and church, losing it loses everything.
